I asked @richardquest if he sees a pattern in Trump’s seemingly market-timed statements on the Iran war:

“Jim, from where I come from, in northern England, we have a saying, let's call a spade a bloody shovel. And and you just got to call it as it as it appears. And here there is no doubt that when the heat gets really hard in the market, something happens. The president says something, he acts. There is a movement that takes the heat out and the market rallies back up again, but nothing fundam

President Trump again delays new strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure, this time for ten days:

“As per Iranian Government request, please let this statement serve to represent that I am pausing the period of Energy Plant destruction by 10 Days to Monday, April 6, 2026, at 8 P.M., Eastern Time. Talks are ongoing and, despite erroneous statements to the contrary by the Fake News Media, and others, they are going very well,” the president posted on Truth Social.

He seemed to hint at that in the WH today


Jonathan Lemire (@JonLemire)

NEW: Trump’s Greenland obsession strained the NATO alliance

Now the Strait of Hormuz could break it

Trump is livid that other nations won’t help. And NATO is bracing for revenge:

Could Trump pull U.S troops out of Europe? Or withdraw from NATO entirely? theatlantic.com/national-sec…




— https://nitter.net/JonLemire/status/2037206739263619181#m

At a time when U.S. troops are at war, a cabinet meeting billed as an update on Iran floated from the Kennedy Center to renovations at the federal reserve to Sharpie pens. President Trump’s most substantive comments on Iran were his view that it wants a deal, without explaining why he believes this, and revealing the “gift” Tehran gave was allowing a few ships through the Strait, in effect acknowledging Iran still maintains control.
Trump reveals the “gift” Iran gave the U.S. was allowing  “eight big boats” to transit the Strait of Hormuz
The cabinet meeting on the Iran war has diverted to the president discussing Sharpie pens
VP Vance just suggested the potential threat of a suicide vest that could kill tens of thousands of people. Not clear if this was rhetorical.

What is the strategic consistency in appeasing Russia while it threatens Europe and going to war with Iran as it threatens the Mideast? Each is surrounded by U.S. allies and each has attacked U.S. allies. Moreover, Russia is aiding Iran in the war, including providing intel to attack U.S. forces.
Trump uses the historic phrase “Never forget” to describe his disappointment that NATO didn’t join the US war against Iran.
Multiple air raid warnings in Tel Aviv all morning - incoming Iranian fire. Notable uptick from yesterday.

GOP Congressman says “President Trump wants to appease President Putin.”:


Rep. Don Bacon 🇺🇸✈️🏍️⭐️🎖️ (@RepDonBacon)

President Trump wants to appease President Putin. Most Americans reject it.  We reject Putin.



— https://nitter.net/RepDonBacon/status/2037009794293211534#m

More GOP questions about Iran end goals. Here’s GOP Rep @PeteSessions to me tonight: “This administration is going to have to figure out: what is the goal here? Is the goal here to open back up the strait of hormuz, or is it where Israel's position would be? Or is it to do away with their desire to bomb people?…We should have a better understanding about what is left in an arsenal against not only the United States and our assets there, but also Israel and other friends that we have in the gulf.

I asked Netanyahu’s foreign policy advisor @FalkOphir why Israel is skeptical of U.S.-Iran peace talks. His answer:

“Well, Iran always lies. We've
we've learned that they always lie. But more importantly, our objective is to remove the existential threat posed by this ayatollah regime. The best way of doing that is to remove the regime. Another way of doing that is to decimate their capabilities, decimate their military capabilities until they get to the stone age.”

Must-watch for season-ready baseball fans:


BaseballHistoryNut (@nut_history)

Major League Baseball is aired in the morning for Japan.  So technically they eat breakfast with it being on television.

Here’s their #openingday commercial.  No hyperbole, when I say this, it might be greater than any US MLB commercial I’ve seen.  Well done and worth the watch for any baseball fan.

Even republican lawmakers expressing concern about the administration’s war plans going forward:


Rep. Nancy Mace (@RepNancyMace)

Just walked out of a House Armed Services briefing on Iran. Let me repeat: I will not support troops on the ground in Iran, even more so after this briefing.



— https://nitter.net/RepNancyMace/status/2036842648338579572#m

Iran is back with five of its own conditions for peace. It’s hard to see how the U.S. and Israel agree to these:

•A complete halt to “aggression and assassinations”
•Establishment of concrete mechanisms to ensure the war on Iran does not resume
•Guaranteed and clearly defined payment of war damages and reparations
•The condition that the war is concluded across all fronts and for all Iranian proxies throughout the region (which would require an end to Israel’s attacks on Lebanon that are target

What is the strategic benefit of trashing treaty allies while coddling a Putin client state?


Christopher Miller (@ChristopherJM)
